radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate | Date: 15 Feb 2025 | Institution: Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)
Clinical Indication:
Follow-up assessment after an earlier prostate biopsy. The latest PSA reading is 4.53 ng/mL, and the prior scan carried a PI-RADS 5 rating.
FINDINGS:
Total gland volume registers at 41.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a sharply demarcated hypointense area within the right peripheral zone at the mid-gland level, spanning roughly 12 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restricted diffusion, mirrored by diminished signal on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhancement captures early focal uptake inside the abnormality. Seminal vesicles maintain normal calibre and signal characteristics. Pelvic lymph nodes appear benign. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is evident.
IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid-peripheral zone. Prostate volume 41.0 mL yielding a PSA density of 0.12 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.84312165.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial laboratory screening in late 2022 recorded a PSA level of 3.2 ng/mL, which climbed to 3.4 ng/mL by June 2023. Because of this upward trend, a urology referral was initiated to arrange further assessment and book the initial biopsy.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: Post-consultation update indicates the earlier biopsy established Gleason 3+3 disease. The current PSA measures 3.5 ng/mL. Clinical notes document the ongoing surveillance plan.
